items.label: Security Finding
items.title: IDOR Vulnerability in Faculty Verification SSE Endpoint
items.description:
Discovered an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability in the faculty verification Server-Sent Events (SSE) endpoint.

The endpoint:
/api/faculty/college-verification/stream/{userId}

fails to validate whether the requesting user is authorized to access the provided userId. By modifying the userId parameter, it is possible to access verification data of other users.

The response exposes sensitive information including:
- College name
- Verification status
- Uploaded file names (logo and ID proof)
- Timestamps and system messages

Impact:
- Unauthorized access to user-specific data
- Enumeration of valid user IDs
- Potential exposure of sensitive documents if file paths are predictable
- Scalable data extraction due to streaming (SSE) nature

Proof of Concept:
A Python script using HTTP/2 streaming confirms that valid user data can be retrieved by iterating user IDs.

Root Cause:
- Missing authorization checks
- Direct exposure of object references (userId)
- Lack of access control on SSE endpoint

Suggested Fix:
- Enforce strict authorization checks for userId
- Use UUIDs instead of sequential IDs
- Restrict SSE endpoints to authenticated users
- Avoid exposing sensitive file references

Severity:
High / Critical
